message.content: {"flag": true, "category": "spoof", "why": "A single NYSE print at 09:36:00 shows last 383.18 (-0.58%) while every other venue at the same timestamp quotes ~385.59, an implausible outlier inconsistent with the surrounding smooth quotes."}
message.reasoning:
The feed shows HD around 385.5, then one quote at 09:36:00 with last 383.18, pct -0.58 — that's a ~2.4 point drop, ~0.6%, which is consistent with pct -0.58. Actually 385.5 * 0.9942 = 383.26. So -0.58% is consistent. But it's an outlier vs surrounding quotes at 385.59 same timestamp. Hmm, is that implausible? A 0.6% move within 15 seconds while other venues show 385.59 at the same time — that's a spoof/implausible quote. But it could be a stale/erroneous print. The pct field is self-consistent though. The surrounding quotes at 09:36:00 NASDAQ show 385.59. A single venue printing 383.18 while others at 385.59 is a bad tick — implausible for the instrument. That's a spoof signal.

Hmm, but is it enough? The guidance: "a feed window ('feed') is clean when the quotes move smoothly and headlines are mundane". Here quotes don't move smoothly — one outlier. I'd flag spoof.

Also headline "The trades in a narrow range ahead of the close" at 09:35:30 — odd (ahead of the close at 9:35am), but mundane-ish. The main issue is the outlier print.

I'll flag spoof.
